sourceEvidence.observation: Closed gateway constructor/campaignTransport; no deliverability event service or policy gate.
Campaign parser admits only its fixed business actions, not a bounce event.
Read-model metrics classify Permanent/Transient/complaint; this is not a suppression writer.

The audience union excludes global blocklisted and failed consent/membership checks. Native disabled subscribers can remain in eligible_count and are separately counted in native_disabled_count; this read function alone does not authorize schedule or send.
Schedule revalidates the stored audience fingerprint/version in the same transaction, explicitly refuses native_disabled_count > 0 and an empty eligible audience before scheduled status.
Actual dispatch admission revalidates native subscriber/membership/snapshot before in_flight.
Source proof requires current eligibility/consent/suppressed; source_ineligible/consent_withdrawn/suppressed stop reasons remain separate.
Campaign preparation preserves tracking policy, links and dispatch identity. House bounce policy must not rewrite this payload.
Audience review distinguishes eligible_count from native_disabled_count. Default audienceReview validation refuses disabled recipients; the final SQL schedule gate independently refuses them.

humanRule.hardBounce: One authenticated and correlated hard bounce requires immediate brand-owned suppression. Never delete history or auto-unblock.
humanRule.softBounce: Required configurable limit; count unique original dispatch attempts for this brand/recipient, not webhook deliveries. Counts are cumulative and delivered events do not reset them.
humanRule.configuration: Initial limit supplied by trusted server code. Later changes require a separately authorized, idempotent journal entry; increasing a limit never auto-unblocks existing suppression.

candidateDesign.storage: No storage implementation or persistence of JSON is supplied. Immutable brand-owned journal state is an internal domain value only. The future repository belongs to the already planned own central database, is absent by default and must atomically append/CAS against its original revision/history hash; no new SQLite database, sidecar service or empty-state fallback.
candidateDesign.authenticity: Required trusted authenticate-and-classify callback mints a private WeakMap-owned event token. Caller verified:true flags, unknown types and foreign-brand tokens are refused. The callback must itself prove original-attempt correlation; the domain module cannot independently attest a provider or dispatch that it does not own. No provider-specific normalizer is included.
candidateDesign.identity: Opaque recipient reference only. Trusted adapter must resolve canonical address/brand membership and correlate the original unique dispatch attempt. Raw addresses, provider payloads and credential values are not journaled or returned.
candidateDesign.dedup: Event identity scoped by brand+provider; original attempt identity scoped by brand+recipient and shared across provider notifications. Identical events no-op; changed event identity bindings conflict; multiple soft events for one attempt count once.
candidateDesign.history: Hash-linked append-only observations and authorized configuration records. Sticky hard/soft suppression, no unblock/delete endpoint. Hash integrity is not authentication of external storage.
candidateDesign.decision: Local suppression requirement is an additional veto, never send authorization. Provider suppression confirmation, worker suspension and tracking state remain untouched.

requiredFutureHooks.contract: Inject a reviewed deliverability service through the private constructor, default absent. A new dedicated authenticated event handler must preserve signed raw body until verification, correlate brand/recipient/attempt from trusted existing dispatch custody, admit the token, and atomically commit the journal/decision before acknowledging. Existing browser proxy routes and READ credentials do not authorize provider events. No handler is added by this candidate.

requiredFutureHooks.source: Native schedule/dispatch admission in campaign-provider.sql and segment-regular-delivery.sql
requiredFutureHooks.contract: Compose current consent/global suppression/worker suspension/frequency gates with the brand-owned house suppression veto in the same final claim transaction. Recheck after audience review and before outbound transport; preserve finish/outcome_unknown and original tracking/idempotency keys. BFF scheduling alone cannot enforce this for independent workers.

Bind the durable policy revision/history hash and current local suppression into the trusted eligibility proof/review. Invalidate stale eligibility when it changes. Do not clear upstream blocklisted status or mutate global Listmonk subscriber status for an address shared across brands.

primaryDocumentation.providedFinding: Listmonk Settings Bounces exposes soft/hard thresholds and actions.
primaryDocumentation.restriction: Deployed provider version and legacy webhook type semantics remain unverified; the candidate consumes only separately authenticated normalized classification and does not configure Listmonk or n8n.

proofLimits: No operational provider classifier, durable repository, inbound HTTP handler, dispatch gate or callback receipt exists in this delivery.
Raw provider classification, signature format, attempt correlation and deployed provider version need native evidence before an adapter is admitted.
Missing/corrupt/full ledger or unknown ingestion result must fail closed at future dispatch admission; never recreate an empty state or consider an event confirmed.
Runtime package, DB schema, least role and migrations are outside this source-only candidate. No new database/service is created.
The local count and suppression are domain requirements, not an observation that a provider status changed. No callback acknowledgment or final dispatch gate is confirmed.

createPolicy.softBounceAttempts: Explicit safe integer 1..100; no default threshold.
createPolicy.providers: 1..8 trusted classifier names, immutable private allowlist.
createPolicy.operationalDefault: No operational verifier, provider adapter, repository or route is supplied.

normalizedEvent.recipientRef: Opaque lowercase SHA256-shaped reference supplied by trusted own brand identity; never an address from the request.
normalizedEvent.attemptId: Stable ORIGINAL dispatch attempt identity shared across notifications/providers; a webhook notification ID is not a dispatch attempt.
normalizedEvent.occurredAt: Nonnegative safe UTC epoch milliseconds, not future; authenticated late hard events still suppress.
callbackObligations: Verify source/raw-body authentication and deployed version/type mapping.
Resolve the brand and recipient through owned dispatch custody; reject ambiguous identity or a mismatched original attempt.
Return a fresh closed immutable classification after successful verification, never trust request verified flags.

methods.initialState: Only for a newly provisioned own brand policy in trusted storage; never after load failure.
methods.admitEvent: Async private classifier invocation; returns only a private process-owned admission token, TTL <300000ms. Token serialization or transfer to another policy is not supported.
methods.admitPolicyChange: Async private authorization of frozen brand/UUID/threshold; requires separate actor authority, not provider event authority.
methods.apply: Synchronous pure transition; validates scope and hash-linked history, deduplicates immutable events/operations, returns next state and local veto. Never commits or acknowledges.
methods.inspect: Synchronous current decision for one owned recipient; never grants send permission.

journal.persistedIdentifierForm: Only opaque recipient/actor references and event/attempt/operation hashes; no raw email, original IDs, provider body or credential.
journal.integrityBoundary: Hash chain detects inconsistency but does not authenticate a state supplied externally. A trusted repository/CAS must retain the admitted state and enforce no rollback or replacement.
journal.restartProof: Tests replay an in-memory JSON encoding of synthetic data; no file/database/store was created and no production restart was proved.

requiredFutureRepositoryInterface.database: Already planned own central database only; native least-role/schema admission remains separate.
requiredFutureRepositoryInterface.admission: Private server constructor owns this interface. It must never accept state, brand ownership, callbacks, threshold authority or verifier functions from HTTP/environment arbitrary input.
requiredFutureRepositoryInterface.commit: Append and compare revisions atomically; a conflict reloads original state and re-applies the same admitted immutable event, never invents another send attempt.
requiredFutureRepositoryInterface.unknown: Missing, corrupt, full, uncertain load/commit or unavailable repository refuses acknowledgment/dispatch and preserves the original event/operation for recovery.
